scope: Checkpoint ledger of claimed complete resolutions and separately asked subparts. Not independent acceptance or a novelty certificate.

candidates.result: A parameter-free definable two-element set generating an infinite subgroup
candidates.original_statement:
A first order formula φ(x) in the group language with one free variable is
said to be concise in a class C of groups if for every group G in C such that the set
Gφ of elements in G satisfying φ is finite, the subgroup φ(G) generated by Gφ is also
finite (cf. 21.105 and Archive 2.45). Is every formula with one free variable concise
in the class of residually finite groups?                               M. Petschick

candidates.result: The p-Jordan infimum need not be attained
candidates.original_statement:
Let p be a prime number. A group Γ is called p-Jordan if there exist
constants J and e such that any finite subgroup G ⊂ Γ contains a normal abelian
subgroup of order coprime to p and of index at most J · |G(p) |e . (For example by the
results of Brauer–Feit and Larsen–Pink, for any field K of characteristic p the group
GLn (K) is p-Jordan with e = 3.) Let the p-Jordan exponent e(Γ) of the group Γ be
the infimum of all constants e for which the above bound holds for some constant
J = J(e).
    a) Is it true that this infimum is always attained?
    b) Is it true that e(Γ) ⩽ 3 for any p-Jordan group Γ?                  C. Shramov

candidates.result: A semi-abelian non-monomial group of order 2592
candidates.original_statement:
A finite group G is said to be semi-abelian if it has a sequence of subgroups
1 = G0 ⩽ G1 ⩽ · · · ⩽ Gn = G such that for every i the subgroup Gi+1 is isomorphic
to a quotient of a semidirect product Ai ⋊ Gi for some abelian group Ai .
    Conjecture: Semi-abelian finite groups are monomial.                     M. Kida

candidates.result: Maximal test rank at every finite rank in a nonabelian nonperiodic variety
candidates.original_statement:
Let M be a variety of groups and let Gr be a free r-generator group in M. A
subset S ⊆ Gr is called a test set if every endomorphism of Gr identical on S is an
automorphism. The minimum of the cardinalities of test sets is called the test rank
of Gr . Suppose that the test rank of Gr is r for every r ⩾ 1.
   a) Is it true that M is an abelian variety?
   b) Suppose that M is not a periodic variety. Is it true that M is the variety of all
abelian groups?                                                      E. I. Timoshenko

104                                 16th Issue (2006)

candidates.result: A torsion-free complex linear group not residually rational in the same degree
candidates.original_statement:
Is it true that every finitely generated torsion-free subgroup of GLn (C) is
residually in the class of torsion-free subgroups of GLn (Q)?          G. A. Noskov

candidates.result: A closed set whose every power greater than one is nonclosed
candidates.original_statement:
Let G be a connected linear reductive algebraic group over a field of positive
characteristic, X a closed subset of G, and let X k = {x1 · · · xk | xi ∈ X}.
    a) Is it true that there always exists a positive integer c = c(X) > 1 such that X c
is closed?
    b) If X is a conjugacy class of G such that X 2 contains an open subset of G, then
is X 2 = G?                                                                 E. P. Vdovin

candidates.result: Failure of the stated finite isolated-radical presentation
candidates.original_statement:
Prove that any irreducible system of equations S(x1 , . . . , xn ) = 1 with
coefficients in a torsion-free linear group G is equivalent over G to a finite sys-
tem T (x1 , . .√  . , xn ) = 1 satisfying an analogue of Hilbert’s Nullstellensatz, i. e.
RadG (T ) = T . This is true if G is a free group (O. Kharlampovich, A. Myasnikov,
J. Algebra, 200 (1998), 472–570).
    Here both S and T are regarded as subsets of G[X] = G ∗ F (X), a free prod-
uct of G and a free group on X = {x1 , . . . , xn }. By definition, RadG (T ) =
{w(x1 , . . . , xn ) ∈ G[X] |√w(g1 , . . . , gn ) = 1 for any solution g1 , . . . , gn ∈ G of the
system T (X) = 1}, and T is the minimal normal isolated subgroup of G[X] con-
taining T .                            G. Baumslag, A. G. Myasnikov, V. N. Remeslennikov

candidates.result: A finite modular nondistributive dominion lattice
candidates.original_statement:
Let M be a quasivariety of groups. The dominion domM       A (H) of a subgroup
H of a group A (in M ) is the set of all elements a ∈ A such that for any two
homomorphisms f, g : A → B ∈ M , if f, g coincide on H, then f (a) = g(a). Suppose
that the set {domN A (H) | N is a quasivariety, N ⊆ M } forms a lattice with respect to
set-theoretic inclusion. Can this lattice be modular and non-distributive? A. I. Budkin

candidates.result: Infinite axiomatic rank of the Klein bottle quasivariety
candidates.original_statement:
Can the quasivariety generated by the group ⟨a, b | a−1 ba = b−1 ⟩ be defined
by a set of quasi-identities in a finite set of variables? The answer is known for all
other groups with one defining relation.                                  A. I. Budkin

candidates.result: Every group representation has a homogeneous extension
candidates.original_statement:
According to P. Hall, a group G is said to be homogeneous if every iso-
morphism of its finitely generated subgroups is induced by an automorphism of G.
It is known (Higman–Neumann–Neumann) that every group is embeddable into a
homogeneous one. Is the same true for the category of representations of groups?
A representation (V, G) is finitely generated if G is a finitely generated group, and V
a finitely generated module over the group algebra of G.                    B. I. Plotkin

candidates.result: A nonsplit additive division-ring extension
candidates.original_statement:
Let A be a division ring, G a subgroup of the multiplicative group of A, and
E an extension of the additive group of A by G such that G acts by multiplication
in A. Is it true that E splits? This is true if G is finite.         E. A. Palyutin.

126                                 18th Issue (2014)

candidates.result: Non-algebraic and non-modular complete lattices of formations
candidates.original_statement:
A non-empty set θ of formations is called a complete lattice of formations
if the intersection of any set of formations in θ belongs to θ and θ has the largest
element (with respect to inclusion).
                               W      If L is a complete lattice, then anWelement a ∈ L
is said to be compact if a ⩽ X for any X ⊆ L implies that a ⩽ X1 for some
finite X1 ⊂ X. A complete lattice is called algebraic if every element is the join of a
(possibly infinite) set of compact elements.
    a) Is there a non-algebraic complete lattice of formations of finite groups?
    b) Is there a non-modular complete lattice of formations of finite groups?
                                                                               A. N. Skiba

candidates.result: A centerless group of order 605 with a multiple-holomorph quotient element of order four
candidates.original_statement:
The holomorph Hol(G) of a group G can be defined as the normalizer of
the subgroup of left translations in the group of all permutations of the set G. The
multiple holomorph NHol(G) of G is the normalizer of the holomorph. Set T (G) =
NHol(G)/Hol(G).
    a) Is there a centerless group G for which T (G) is not an elementary abelian
2-group?
    b) Is there a finite centerless group G for which T (G) is not an elementary abelian
2-group?
    c) (A. Caranti). Is there a finite p-group G for which the order of T (G) has a
prime divisor not dividing (p − 1)p?                                           C. Tsang

candidates.result: A two-generator infinite profinite CA-group mapping onto A5
candidates.original_statement:
A profinite group in which all centralizers of non-trivial elements are pronilpo-
tent is called a CN-group. Find an example of a finitely generated infinite profinite
CN-group which is not prosoluble.
   The structure of profinite CN-groups is described in (P. Shumyatsky, Israel
J. Math., 235, no. 1 (2020), 325–347).                                   P. Shumyatsky

candidates.result: Finite subgroup-lattice dimension for the specified Chernikov groups
candidates.original_statement:
The dimension of a partially ordered set ⟨P, ⩽⟩ is, by definition, the least
cardinal number δ such that the relation ⩽ is an intersection of δ relations of linear
order on P . Is it true that, for any Chernikov group which does not contain a direct
product of two quasicyclic groups over the same prime number, the subgroup lattice
has finite dimension? Expected answer: yes.                             L. N. Shevrin

candidates.result: A smooth affine surface with a smooth fixed divisor and a singular cyclic quotient
candidates.original_statement:
Let X be a regular algebraic variety over a field of arbitrary characteristic,
and G a finite cyclic group of automorphisms of X. Suppose that the fixed point
variety X G of G is a regular hypersurface of X (of codimension 1). Is the quotient
variety X/G regular?                                               K. N. Ponomarëv

candidates.result: Virtual nilpotence of rational linear groups with finitely many automorphism orbits
candidates.original_statement:
Let G be a subgroup of GL(n, Q) with finitely many orbits under automor-
phisms. Is G a virtually soluble group?                    A. Dantas, E. de Melo

candidates.result: An order-twelve counterexample to the semiperfectness criterion
candidates.original_statement:
Let G be a finite group, Z(p) the localization at p, and Fp the field of p elements.
Let X be the class of Fp G-modules obtained by reduction of simple QG-modules.
Is it true that Z(p) G is semiperfect if and only if each projective indecomposable
Fp G-module can be written as an N-linear combination of modules in X inside the
Grothendieck group of Fp G?
    The “only if” direction is proved, and the affirmative answer is obtained if p does
not divide |G| (D. Johnston, D. Rumynin, J. Algebra, 687, no. 1 (2026), 776–791).
                                                               D. Johnston, D. Rumynin

candidates.result: Non-unique indecomposable projective decompositions over Z_(5)[3.A7]
candidates.original_statement:
Let G be a finite group, and Z(p) the localization at p. Can every projective
Z(p) G-module be uniquely, up to permutations and isomorphisms, written as a direct
sum of indecomposable projective Z(p) G-modules?
   It is known that the category of finitely generated projective Z(p) G-modules is not
a Krull–Schmidt category (S. M. Woods, Canadian J. Math., 26, no. 1 (1974), 121–
129). See also (D. Johnston, D. Rumynin, J. Algebra, to appear, https://arxiv.org/
pdf/2507.21316).                                                    K. W. Roggenkamp

candidates.result: A countable resolvable group without an expansive sequence
candidates.original_statement:
A sequence {Fn } of pairwise disjoint finite subsets of a topological group is
called expansive if for every open subset U there is a number m such that Fn ∩ U ̸= ∅
for all n > m. Suppose that a countable group G can be partitioned into countably
many dense subsets. Is it true that in G there exists an expansive sequence? Cf. 15.80.
                                                                         I. V. Protasov

candidates.result: An infinite four-regular Cayley graph with invertible adjacency on all functions
candidates.original_statement:
Let Γ be an infinite undirected connected vertex-symmetric graph of finite
valency without loops or multiple edges. Is it true that every complex number is an
eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of Γ under its natural action as a linear operator
on the complex vector space of all complex-valued functions on the vertex set of Γ?
                                                                            V. I. Trofimov

candidates.result: An exact cubic-time minimum-palindrome-factorization algorithm in free groups
candidates.original_statement:
An element g of a free group Fn on the free generators x1 , . . . , xn is called a
palindrome with respect to these generators if the reduced word representing g is the
same when read from left to right or from right to left. The palindromic length of an
element w ∈ Fn is the smallest number of palindromes in Fn whose product is w. Is
there an algorithm for finding the palindromic length of a given element of Fn ?
                                        V. G. Bardakov, V. A. Tolstykh, V. E. Shpilrain

98                                   16th Issue (2006)

candidates.result: Non-enumerability of both the cofinite finite-group theory and its complement
candidates.original_statement:
Mal’cev proved that the set of sentences that hold in all finite groups is not
computably enumerable, although its complement is. Is it true that both the set of
sentences that hold in almost all finite groups and its complement are not computably
enumerable?                                                           O. V. Belegradek

candidates.result: Solubility from the restricted coprime-commutator order condition
candidates.original_statement:
A ⋆-commutator is a commutator [x, y] of two elements x, y of coprime prime-
power orders. Is a finite group G soluble if |ab| ⩾ |a||b| for any ⋆-commutators a and
b of coprime orders?                                                    V. S. Monakhov

candidates.result: The printed brace average is pre-Lie for every uniformly sufficiently large prime
candidates.original_statement:
This question is about existence of an analogue of the Lazard correspondence
for pre-Lie algebras and braces. A pre-Lie algebra A is a vector space with a bilinear
operation (x, y) → xy satisfying (xy)z − x(yz) = (yx)z − y(xz) for every x, y, z ∈ A.
A pre-Lie algebra A is said to be left nilpotent if, for some n ∈ N, A·(A·(A · · · A))) = 0
where A appears n times in the product. Recall that a set A with binary operations +
and ◦ is a left brace if (A, +) is an abelian group, (A, ◦) is a group, and a ◦ (b + c) + a =
a ◦ b + a ◦ c for every a, b, c ∈ A. Let p be a prime, and Fp the field of p elements.
A left brace A is called an Fp -brace if its additive group is an Fp -vector space such
that a ∗ (αb) = α(a ∗ b) for all a, b ∈ A, α ∈ Fp , where a ∗ b = a ◦ b − a − b. The idea of
a connection between braces and pre-Lie algebras comes from a paper by W. Rump
(2014).
    a) Let A be an Fp -brace of cardinality pk for some k. Is it true that when p is
sufficiently large relative to k, the set
                                       PA   with the same additive operation + and with
                                          p−2
the operation · defined as a · b = − i=0 21i ((2i a) ∗ b) is a pre-Lie algebra?
                                      n−1
    Comment of 2025: If 2 ≡ ξ p            when ξ is a primitive root modulo p, and if
A is strongly nilpotent of nilpotency index less than p, then the result follows by
(A. Smoktunowicz, Adv. Math., 409, part B (2022), 108683). It is not known if the
result follows when A is not strongly nilpotent.
  ∗ b) Let k be a natural number, and let p be a prime number such that p > 2k . Is
there a bijective correspondence between Fp -braces of cardinality pk and left nilpotent
pre-Lie algebras over Fp of cardinality pk ?
   An affirmative answer to any of the above questions would have consequences for
the theory of set-theoretic solutions of the Yang–Baxter equation and for the theory
of Hopf–Galois extensions.                                            A. Smoktunowicz
  ∗ b) Yes, there is (S. Trappeniers, Preprint, 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.
02475).

candidates.result: A height-four scattered compact space excluded from the stated E-spaces
candidates.original_statement:
Is it true that every scattered compact can be homeomorphically embedded
into the space of all closed non-compact subgroups with E-topology of a suitable
locally compact group?                                            I. V. Protasov

candidates.result: An explicit criterion for orthogonal bases in every dimension
candidates.original_statement:
Let a be a vector in Rn with rational coordinates and set
                          S(a) = {ka + b | k ∈ Z, b ∈ Zn }.
It is obvious that S(a) is a discrete subgroup in Rn of rank n. Find necessary and
sufficient conditions in terms of the coordinates of a for S(a) to have an orthogonal
basis with respect to the standard scalar product in Rn .
                                                           Yu. D. Popov, I. V. Protasov

                                  9th Issue (1984)                                    35

candidates.result: A three-generated perfect periodic group with one involution class and odd pairwise products
candidates.original_statement:
Construct an example of a (periodic) group without subgroups of index 2
which is generated by a conjugacy class of involutions X such that the order of the
product of any two involutions from X is odd.                         A. I. Sozutov

candidates.result: An explicit logarithmic degree bound for symmetric-group power-word universality
candidates.original_statement:
A group word is said to be universal on a group G if its values on G run
over the whole of G. For an arbitrary constant c > 8/5, J. L. Brenner, R. J. Evans,
and D. M. Silberger (Proc. Amer. Math. Soc., 96, no. 1 (1986), 23–28) proved that
there exists a number N0 = N0 (c) such that the word xr y s , rs ̸= 0, is universal on
the alternating group An for any n ⩾ max {N0 , c · log m(r, s)}, where m(r, s) is the
product of all primes dividing rs if r, s ̸∈ {−1, 1}, and m(r, s) = 1 if r, s ∈ {−1, 1}.
For example, one can take N0 (5/2) = 5 and N0 (2) = 29. Find an analogous bound
for the degree of the symmetric group Sn under hypothesis that at least one of the r, s
is odd: up to now, here only a more crude bound n ⩾ max {6, 4m(r, s) − 4} is known
(M. Droste, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc., 96, no. 1 (1986), 18–22).        Yu. I. Merzlyakov

candidates.result: Nonrationality of the stated classical cyclic and semisimple limits
candidates.original_statement:
A square matrix is said to be separable if its minimal polynomial has no
repeated roots, and cyclic if its minimal and characteristic polynomials are equal.
For a matrix group G over a finite field define s(G) and c(G) to be the proportion
of separable and of cyclic elements respectively in G. For a classical group X(d, q) of
dimension d defined over the field with q elements let S(X; q) := limd→∞ s(X(d, q))
and C(X; q) := limd→∞ c(X(d, q)). Independently G. E. Wall (Bull. Austral. Math.
Soc., 60, no. 2 (1999), 253–284) and J. Fulman (J. Group Theory, 2, no. 3 (1999),
251–289) have evaluated S(GL; q) and C(GL; q), and have found them to be rational
functions of q. Are S(X; q) and C(X; q) rational functions of q also for the unitary,
symplectic, and orthogonal groups?                                      P. M. Neumann

92                                  15th Issue (2002)

candidates.result: Continuum many infinite alternating-residual quotients of every triangle group Delta(2,3,r), r>6
candidates.original_statement:
A group x, y | xl = y m = (xy)n is called the triangle group with parame-
ters (l, m, n). It is proved in (A. M. Brunner, R. G. Burns, J. Wiegold, Math. Sci-
entist, 4 (1979), 93–98) that the triangle group (2, 3, 30) has uncountably many
non-isomorphic homomorphic images that are residually finite alternating groups. Is
the same true for the triangle group (2, 3, n) for all n > 6?            J. Wiegold

candidates.result: A periodic group with Sylow two-subgroups of order two and noncentral involutions modulo the odd-order radical
candidates.original_statement:
Let G be a periodic group containing an involution i and suppose that the
Sylow 2-subgroups of G are either locally cyclic or generalized quaternion. Does the
element iO2′ (G) of the factor-group G/O2′ (G) always lie in its centre?
                                                                           V. P. Shunkov

                                                                                      15



              Problems from the 5th Issue (1976)

candidates.result: No finite quasigroup generates the ordinary isotope variety of a nontrivial finite group
candidates.original_statement:
It is known that if M is a variety (quasivariety, pseudovariety) of groups, then
the class IM of all quasigroups that are isotopic to groups in M is also a variety
(quasivariety, pseudovariety), and IM is finitely based if and only if M is finitely
based. Is it true that if M is generated by a single finite group then IM is generated
by a single finite quasigroup?                                         A. A. Gvaramiya

candidates.result: Unbounded Brauer-degree p-parts with the group-order p-part fixed
candidates.original_statement:
Let φ be an irreducible p-modular character of a finite group G. Find the
best-possible estimate of the form φ(1)p ⩽ f (|G|p ). Here np is the p-part of a positive
integer n.                                                             A. S. Kondratiev

                                 12th Issue (1992)                                   61

candidates.result: A free nilpotent group with a Z[t]-completion that is not locally nilpotent
candidates.original_statement:
Prove that the tensor A-completion (see A. G. Myasnikov, V. N. Remeslenni-
kov, Siberian Math. J., 35, no. 5 (1994), 986–996) of a free nilpotent group can be
non-nilpotent.                                A. G. Myasnikov, V. N. Remeslennikov

candidates.result: Closure of the torsion-free nilpotent quasivariety under restricted wreath products with Z
candidates.original_statement:
A quasivariety M is closed under direct Z-wreath products if the direct wreath
product G ≀ Z belongs to M for every G ∈ M (here Z is an infinite cyclic group).
Is the quasivariety generated by the class of all nilpotent torsion-free groups closed
under direct Z-wreath products?                                            A. I. Budkin

candidates.result: Innerness of category automorphisms for full varieties of groups of fixed derived length
candidates.original_statement:
b) If Θ is a variety of groups, then let Θ0 denote the category of all free groups
of finite rank in Θ. It is proved (G. Mashevitzky, B. Plotkin, E. Plotkin J. Algebra,
282 (2004), 490–512) that if Θ is the variety of all groups, then every automorphism
of the category Θ0 is an inner one. The same is true if Θ is the variety of all nilpotent
groups of class ⩽ d, for d ⩾ 2 (A. Tsurkov, Int. J. Algebra Comput., 17 (2007),
1273–1281). Is this true for the varieties of solvable groups? of metabelian groups?
    An automorphism φ of a category is called inner if it is isomorphic to the identity
automorphism. Let s : 1 → φ be a function defining this isomorphism. Then for
every object A we have an isomorphism sA : A → φ(A) and for any morphism of
objects µ : A → B we have φ(µ) = sB µs−1   A .                              B. I. Plotkin

candidates.result: Periodicity of subgroups contained in a product of periodic subgroups in a soluble group
candidates.original_statement:
Let G be a soluble group, and let A and B be periodic subgroups of G. Is
it true that any subgroup of G contained in the set AB = {ab | a ∈ A, b ∈ B} is
periodic? This is known to be true if AB is a subgroup of G.      F. de Giovanni

candidates.result: Unbounded lower p-central factors in the specified two-generator finite p-groups
candidates.original_statement:
Conjecture: There exists a function f : N × N → N such that, if G is a finite
p-group with d generators and G has no epimorphic images isomorphic to the wreath
product Cp ≀ Cp , then each factor of the p-lower central series of G has order bounded
above by f (p, d).
   It is interesting to compare this conjecture with the celebrated characterization of
Aner Shalev of finitely generated p-adic analytic pro-p-groups.                  P. Spiga

candidates.result: The insoluble totally two-closed group J1 times C13 with Fitting subgroup C13
candidates.original_statement:
For k ⩾ 1, a group G is said to be totally k-closed if in each of its faithful
permutation representations, say on a set Ω, G is the largest subgroup of Sym(Ω)
which leaves invariant each of the G-orbits in the induced action on the set of ordered
k-tuples Ωk .
   Are there any finite insoluble totally 2-closed groups with nontrivial Fitting sub-
group?
   The finite totally 2-closed groups which are either soluble or have trivial Fitting
subgroup are known.      M. Arezoomand, M. A. Iranmanesh, C. E. Praeger, G. Tracey

candidates.result: Every derived elementary carpet is closed
candidates.original_statement:
Let A = {Ar | r ∈ Φ} be an elementary carpet of type  P Φ of rank         l ⩾ 2 (see
7.28). For p ∈ Φ, define a set of additive subgroups Bp =       Cij,rs Air Ajs , where the
sum is taken over all natural numbers i, j and roots r, s ∈ Φ such that ir + js = p. It
is known that the set B = {Bp | p ∈ Φ} is a carpet called the derived carpet of A. It
is also known that for Φ = Al the set B is a closed (admissible) carpet, which means
that its carpet subgroup does not contain new root elements. Is every derived carpet
of type Φ over a commutative ring closed (admissible)?
    Comment of 2025: An affirmative answer was obtained for Φ of type Bl , Cl , or
F4 when GCD(p, 2) = 1, and for Φ of type G2 when GCD(p, 6) = 1 (Ya. N. Nuzhin,
J. Siberian Fed. Univ. Ser. Math. Phys., 16, no. 6 (2023), 732–737). Ya. N. Nuzhin

140                                     19th Issue (2018)

candidates.result: Every carpet closure is a carpet with unchanged derived carpet
candidates.original_statement:
Let A = {Ar | r ∈ Φ} be an elementary carpet of type Φ over a commutative
ring K (see 7.28), and let Φ(A) = ⟨xr (Ar ) | r ∈ Φ⟩ be its carpet subgroup. Define the
closure of the carpet A to be the set of additive subgroups A = {Ar | r ∈ Φ}, where
Ar = {t ∈ K | xr (t) ∈ Φ(A)}. Is the closure A of a carpet A always a carpet?
    An affirmative answer is known if Φ = Al , Dl , El .                  Ya. N. Nuzhin

candidates.result: Irreducible closed noncompletable nets of every order in every odd characteristic
candidates.original_statement:
Let σ = (σij ), 1 ⩽ i ̸= j ⩽ n, be an irreducible elementary net (carpet)
of order n ⩾ 3 over a field K (see 19.48). The net σ is said to be closed if the
elementary net subgroup E(σ) does not contain new elementary transvections. The
net σ is said to be completable if its diagonal can be supplemented with subgroups
to a complete net. Completable elementary nets are closed. It is known that over
fields of characteristic 0 and 2 there exist irreducible closed elementary nets that are
not completable (V. A. Koibaev, Trudy Inst. Mat. Mekh. Ural Div. Ross. Akad.
Nauk, 17, no. 4 (2011), 134–141 (Russian); V. A. Koibaev, Siberian Math. J., 62,
no. 2 (2021), 262–266).
    Do there exist irreducible closed elementary nets of order n ⩾ 3 over a field of odd
characteristic that are not completable?                                  V. A. Koibaev

candidates.result: Proper-power normal closures with equal commutator subgroups
candidates.original_statement:
Suppose that X is a free non-cyclic group, N is a non-trivial normal subgroup
of X and T is a proper subgroup of X containing N . Is it true that [T, N ] < [X, N ]
if N is not maximal in X?                                               V. P. Shaptala

candidates.result: Minimum-order intersections outside the Fitting subgroup in a soluble wreath group
candidates.original_statement:
For nilpotent subgroups A, B, C of a finite group G, let MinG (A, B, C)
be the subgroup of A generated by all minimal by inclusion intersections of the form
A∩B x ∩C y , where x, y ∈ G, and let minG (A, B, C) be the subgroup of MinG (A, B, C)
generated by all intersections of this kind of minimal order.
    a) Is it true that minG (A, B, C) ⩽ F (G)?
    b) Is it true that MinG (A, B, C) ⩽ F (G)?
    c) The same questions for soluble groups.                            V. I. Zenkov

candidates.result: Unbounded numbers of system normalizers, with fixed Frattini order three
candidates.original_statement:
Is there a positive integer n such that the hypercenter of any finite soluble
group coincides with the intersection of n system normalizers of that group? What is
